text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan signs a National Security Council (NSC) statement aimed at countering Islamist activism after resisting for several days.
- Parties in parliament, excluding Erbakan's Islamist Welfare Party, call for the introduction of eight-year compulsory education.
- Ankara is shocked by the comment of a German official rejecting the possibility of Turkey appearing in the European Union family photo.
- The National Security Council's decisions are to be discussed by the cabinet of ministers.
- Prime Minister Erbakan concealed from Islamists his signing of the NSC statement.
- A parliamentary commission investigating a security scandal decides to question Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller and her family.
- The construction of a gas pipeline from Egypt to Turkey is proposed as an alternative to a planned Iran-Turkey pipeline, which has drawn criticism from the United States.
- The directorate of religious affairs denies pupils were made to swear in Koran courses to fight for the establishment of an Islamist state.
